item.title: Misleading Traffic Signs, Excessive Sign Clutter and Road Safety Concerns, 26th November
item.description:
Location: Cornwall Road, junction with Gorleston Road and Falmer Road, London N15. As a DVSA Approved Driving Instructor with approximately 15 years of professional experience and over 80,000 hours of road experience, I wish to raise serious concerns regarding this junction. The positioning of five No Motor Vehicles signs, two camera enforcement signs and directional road markings creates unnecessary ambiguity regarding the permitted route. The first prohibition sign is positioned before the right-turning point, while another is positioned adjacent to Falmer Road. This arrangement can create the impression that proceeding in either direction constitutes a contravention, while reversing raises further safety concerns. Excessive signage may also increase cognitive overload, particularly for inexperienced motorists and drivers with neurodivergent conditions, special educational needs or information-processing difficulties. Please investigate this arrangement with reference to: * Regulation 18 of the Local Authorities’ Traffic Orders Regulations 1996 – adequate communication of traffic restrictions. * Traffic Signs Regulations and General Directions 2016 (TSRGD) – appropriate positioning and application of regulatory signs. * DfT Traffic Signs Manual, Chapter 1, sections 2.1–2.4 – minimising unnecessary signage, duplication, distraction, sign clutter and public expenditure. * Equality Act 2010, Section 149 – Public Sector Equality Duty and consideration of disabled road users. I request a formal highway engineering and road safety review, including the justification for each prohibition sign, cognitive accessibility, value for taxpayers’ money and opportunities to simplify the junction. Traffic management should facilitate safe, clear and predictable compliance rather than create unnecessary uncertainty and repeated enforcement. Please refer this report to the responsible Highway Authority’s Traffic Engineering and Road Safety teams for investigation and provide a reasoned response.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 1, Falmer Road, West Green, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Enfield council gaslighting, 26th November
item.description:

In response to yet another concern Enfield council came and cleaned the two spots of Bourne hill I reported and left the other waste up and down Bourne hill now four weeks or more with no cleaning. The images are not the worst of the evidence their, but the macdonakds packaging evidences waste on Tuesday, allegedly street cleaned but actually not and there today. The other image is the waste collected from Bourne hill which is filthy. The community are cleaning the road on Saturday and filming this to send to a very worrying council
